text: This capstone project used every piece of the Job-Ready Foundation stage, not just this course. How IT Teams Work is why sitting down with Dana Oyelaran to write real requirements felt like a normal first step. Networking, Linux, Virtualization & Cloud Fundamentals is why subnet, VNet, and virtual machine never needed defining when they showed up in Lesson 29 -- the bedrock everything else stood on.

Azure Administration and AWS Administration taught the same ideas -- compute, storage, networking, identity -- in each provider's own vocabulary, which is why Lesson 29's provider choice was a real decision, not a coin flip between two clouds you'd only learned one of. Identity, Networking & Cloud Security is where least-privilege thinking came from directly -- behind every NSG rule and the managed identity that replaced a stored secret entirely.

PowerShell, Python, Azure CLI & Infrastructure Automation is why every command in this project appeared as a script or CLI call instead of portal clicks nobody could repeat. Put together: real requirements, a network deployed first with correct NSGs, compute wired to storage with no stored credential, four alerts that matter, a backup policy tied to a stated RTO and RPO, three restores actually tested, a real bug diagnosed systematically, and documentation written for someone else.

That's the complete job, and this stage is built toward Cloud Support Engineer and Junior Cloud Engineer roles. Triaging one of the four alerts this course taught you to configure, following a runbook someone else wrote, or deploying the next small environment yourself -- network-first order and least-privilege NSGs included -- are no longer abstract skills. "Walk me through a deployment you've done" now has a real answer.

The Job-Ready Foundation stage is complete: seven courses, from how IT teams work through this capstone. Advanced Specialization starts next with Terraform, Bicep & Infrastructure as Code -- declaring what infrastructure should exist and previewing it before it's created, the discipline this course's operational work was always going to lead toward.
